Exact joint inclusion probabilities of the sampled units

Source: R/variance.R
joint_inclusion.Rd

Chromy's procedure run down a fixed list is the same design as ordered pivotal sampling, and for that design the joint (second-order) inclusion probabilities have closed forms (Chauvet and Le Gleut, 2021, Theorem 3); with the random head the design is the mixture of the circular rotations, each weighted by its unit's probability over the sample size (their eq. 5.3) — precisely the head chromy_sample() draws. This function evaluates those forms exactly for the sampled units, making the Sen–Yates–Grundy variance of the Horvitz–Thompson total exact rather than approximated; as_svydesign() with variance = "pps" hands it to the survey package.

Usage

joint_inclusion(x)

Arguments

x

A chromy_sample() drawn with head = "all" (the default) and min_replacement = FALSE (the default).

Value

The symmetric matrix of joint inclusion probabilities of the sampled units, in the order of x$sample, with the first-order (effective) probabilities on the diagonal.

Details

Joint inclusion probabilities belong to the without-replacement design: a sample drawn with min_replacement = TRUE, where a unit may be selected more than once, is refused. The cost is of order N (frame) times the square of the sample size.

References

Chauvet, G. and Le Gleut, R. (2021). Properties of Chromy's sampling procedure. Survey Methodology, 47(2), 321–347.

Examples

set.seed(9)
frame <- data.frame(size = rlnorm(40, 2))
s <- chromy_sample(frame, n = 10, size = "size")
p2 <- joint_inclusion(s)
all(abs(p2 - t(p2)) < 1e-12)
#> [1] TRUE
all(diag(p2) == s$sample$expected_hits)
#> [1] TRUE
